what: The image of the two birds on one tree (RV 1.164.20)

evidence.detail: Quoted verbatim as Muṇḍaka 3.1.1 and Śvetāśvatara 4.6, where the birds become the individual self and the Lord.

what: The two paths of the fathers and of the gods (RV 10.88.15)

evidence.detail: Quoted in Bṛhadāraṇyaka 6.2.2 in the doctrine of the five fires.

what: Vāmadeva's 'I was Manu and the Sun' (RV 4.26.1) and 'in the womb I knew the births of the gods' (4.27.1) as words of realization

evidence.detail: Bṛhadāraṇyaka 1.4.10 and Aitareya Upaniṣad 2.5 cite them as Vāmadeva's realization.

what: The verses on yoking the mind at the start of the fire altar (VS 11.1–5 = TS 4.1.1; RV 5.81.1)

evidence.detail: They open the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad's chapter on yoga (2.1–5).

what: The Puruṣa of RV 10.90 and the 'Uttaranārāyaṇa' verse VS 31.18

evidence.detail: VS 31.18 recurs as Śvetāśvatara 3.8; RV 10.90.1–2 recur in Śvetāśvatara 3.14–15 (second locus from memory).

what: Further Saṃhitā verses quoted in the Upaniṣads: RV 6.47.18 (Indra's māyās), 1.164.39 (the syllable in highest heaven), 4.40.5 (the haṃsa), AVŚ 10.8.27 (you are woman, you are man)
The Atharvaveda's highest Brahman, the self 'knowing whom one does not fear death', the city of Brahman in the body, the Full, and Prāṇa as lord of all

evidence.detail: AVŚ 10.8.44 (the fearless self), 10.2.28–33 (the city of Brahman), 10.8.29 (from the full the full), 11.4 (Prāṇa) have close Upaniṣadic parallels (e.g. BĀU 5.1.1; Praśna 2).
The Kaṭha Upaniṣad (1.3.9) names the end of the road 'that highest step of Viṣṇu'; Vaiṣṇava tradition recites 1.22.20 in worship (tradition-account).

what: The Puruṣa Sūkta as central Vaiṣṇava liturgy (its seer Nārāyaṇa; its sixteen verses for the sixteen offerings)

evidence.detail: Vaiṣṇava worship employs the Puruṣa Sūkta and identifies its seer and subject with Nārāyaṇa.

what: The Śatarudrīya and the formula 'namaḥ śivāya' (TS 4.5.8) as Vedic root of Śaiva worship and of the five-syllable mantra

evidence.detail: Śaiva traditions chant the Rudram in worship and trace the pañcākṣara to TS 4.5.8.
The Jābāla Upaniṣad names the recitation of the śatarudrīya as a means to immortality (reference from memory).

what: RV 10.125 recited as the Devī Sūkta, Speech as the Goddess who is the self of all

evidence.detail: Recited with the Devī Māhātmya in Śākta worship.

what: Ṛgveda verses on speech read as praise of grammar (4.58.3 'four horns'; 10.71.2 and 10.71.4; 1.164.45 'four quarters')

evidence.detail: Patañjali's Mahābhāṣya (Paspaśāhnika) cites 4.58.3 and 10.71.2, 10.71.4 (and, as usually reported, 1.164.45) as reasons for studying grammar; the Nirukta records the grammarians' reading of 1.164.45 as the four word-classes.

what: The Sāman notes and chant as the source of music

evidence.detail: The Nāradīya Śikṣā maps the Sāman notes on the flute's notes (1.5.1–2); the Nāṭyaśāstra (1.17) says Brahmā took song from the Sāmaveda.

what: Atharvavedic healing (bhaiṣajya) and the status of Āyurveda as a limb (upāṅga/upaveda) of the Atharvaveda

evidence.detail: Suśruta Saṃhitā Sūtrasthāna 1.6 calls Āyurveda an upāṅga of the Atharvaveda; Caraka Saṃhitā Sūtrasthāna 30.21 enjoins devotion to the Atharvaveda (loci from memory, moderate).

what: The Sāvitrī (Gāyatrī), with Oṃ and the vyāhṛtis, as the mantra of initiation and of the twilight worship

evidence.detail: Gṛhya and dharma texts prescribe imparting the Sāvitrī at upanayana and its daily repetition (Manusmṛti ch. 2, verse numbers not recalled).

what: The long-haired, wind-girdled, silent muni of RV 10.136

evidence.detail: Some scholars see in the Keśin and munis a current of ecstatic asceticism distinct from the sacrificial priesthood, later related to the śramaṇa and yogic traditions; the direction and even the existence of the borrowing are disputed. Metadata only.

what: The Vrātya who becomes Mahādeva and Īśāna, and Rudra's names Bhava, Śarva, Paśupati in the Atharvaveda

evidence.detail: Some scholars link the vrātyas and the Atharvavedic Rudra to later Śaiva ascetic movements such as the Pāśupatas; disputed. Metadata only.
